:::{#thm-singleton-bound}
#### Singleton bound

Every [block code](#def-block-code) over an alphabet of $q$ symbols,
with message length $k$, block length $n$ and
[minimum distance](#def-hamming-distance) $d$,
satisfies $d \le n - k + 1$.

:::

::: {.proof}
Delete the last $d - 1$ symbols of every codeword.
Two different codewords differ in at least $d$ positions,
so they still differ in one of the first $n - d + 1$ positions.
So the $q^k$ codewords stay distinct as strings of length $n - d + 1$,
of which there are $q^{n - d + 1}$.
Hence $q^k \le q^{n - d + 1}$, that is, $k \le n - d + 1$.

:::
